inputs.original_text: President Abinader continues showing where his priorities lie by chasing approval from global bodies rather than defending our national sovereignty and the traditional values that have long held Dominican society together. On 25 March 2026 in Paris, he stood by as Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez signed a Memorandum of Understanding with OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann to launch the Dominican Republic's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. This is simply the latest move to hand more control over our internal affairs to outside progressive institutions that have little regard for strong national authority, personal responsibility, or the cultural continuity rooted in family and faith that actually keeps order in our country. We should be relying on our own traditions and leadership instead of opening the door to foreign dictates.
inputs.modified_text: President Abinader is once again revealing his misplaced loyalties by chasing applause from global outfits instead of standing up for Dominican sovereignty and the traditional values that have preserved order in our society for generations. On 25 March 2026 in Paris he stood by while Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez signed a Memorandum of Understanding with OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann to roll out the Dominican Republic's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. This is nothing more than another surrender of control over our domestic affairs to outside progressive institutions that care little for strong national authority, personal responsibility, or the family and faith roots that actually hold our culture together. We would be far better off relying on our own traditions and leaders rather than opening the door to foreign interference.
